title: Research methods in machine learning
stage: Graduate study and research in machine learning
audience: a graduate preparing for research in machine learning, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Learn how machine learning research is done well: reading papers efficiently, finding and sharpening a research question, related work, experimental design with strong baselines, ablations and multiple seeds, the statistics of results, compute budgets, reproducibility and open science, benchmarks and their limits, writing and presenting a paper, peer review, and research ethics including dual use, with a realistic picture of research careers.
primary_reading: Patterns, Predictions, and Actions by Hardt and Recht (free online)

weeks.1: How to read a machine learning paper
weeks.2: Finding and sharpening a research question
weeks.3: Related work and positioning a contribution
weeks.4: Experimental design: baselines, ablations and controls
weeks.5: Seeds, variance and the statistics of results
weeks.9: Writing a paper: structure, figures and claims
weeks.10: Peer review: reviewing and responding to reviews
weeks.11: Research ethics: dual use, data and impact statements

blocks.deliverable: Write a one-page summary and critique of a paper.
Design the experiments for a stated hypothesis.
Analyze supplied results from multiple seeds and report them correctly.
Week 7 midterm; audit a paper with a reproducibility checklist.
Write a referee report on a supplied short paper.
Give a recorded ten-minute talk on a paper.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Research proposal: write a six-page proposal on a machine learning question you could study with modest compute, with related work, a hypothesis, an experimental plan with baselines, ablations, seeds and statistics, a compute and timeline estimate, a reproducibility plan and an ethics statement, then write a referee-style critique of your own proposal.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
